title: Prediction Audit & Forecast Scoring — Prior Claims, Probabilities and Hindsight Control
purpose: Give the Prediction / Revelation Room a rigorous forecasting lane alongside its prophecy and interpretation lanes.
epistemic_rule: A symbolic or theological revelation can be meaningful without being a forecast. A forecast becomes auditable only when its target, time horizon, resolution rule and prior wording are fixed before the outcome is known.

forecast_contract.question: What exactly is being predicted?
forecast_contract.resolution_rule: Source and rule that decide whether the outcome occurred.
forecast_contract.probability: Use a probability when the claim is genuinely uncertain rather than only yes/no rhetoric.
forecast_contract.baseline: Record an outside-view/base-rate benchmark where possible.
forecast_contract.update_log: Preserve later probability revisions rather than overwriting the original forecast.
forecast_contract.negative_case: State what would count as a miss.

scoring.brier_score: For binary outcomes, the Brier score is the squared difference between forecast probability and outcome (0 or 1). Lower is better. Proper scoring rules reward honest probabilistic estimates over strategic certainty.
scoring.calibration: Among forecasts assigned probability p, roughly p proportion should resolve true over a sufficiently large sample if the forecaster is calibrated.
scoring.resolution: A forecast should be scored against the rule fixed before resolution; do not change the target after the event.

forecasting_practices: Start with base rates / outside-view frequencies before adding case-specific evidence.
Break broad questions into smaller resolvable components.
Use probabilities rather than false certainty when uncertainty is real.
Update when evidence changes and preserve the update history.
Aggregate independent judgments where useful rather than hiding disagreement.
Keep score across many resolved forecasts; one memorable hit is weak evidence of forecasting skill.

hindsight_bias.definition: Knowledge of an outcome can make the outcome appear more predictable in retrospect than it appeared beforehand.
hindsight_bias.evidence: Close replications published in 2021 found hindsight-bias effects in both retrospective and prospective judgment tasks. A 2025 fifty-year review describes the bias across experimental and real-world settings and emphasizes reconstruction of past perspective as a possible mitigation.
hindsight_bias.archive_consequence: Preserve the exact prior claim, timestamp, confidence and alternatives. Never reconstruct a prior forecast from memory after the outcome.

claim_classes.requirements: prior wording + target + horizon + resolution rule + probability/confidence + outcome
clear prior target and outcome condition but no probability score
claim_classes.status: can be audited hit/miss, but not fully calibrated
first resolve whether X occurred before judging Y

claim_classes.requirements: earlier symbol/pattern predates event but target is broad or ambiguous
temporal or structural relation without prior discriminating claim
claim_classes.status: preserve if culturally/project-relevant; no forecast credit

anti_cherry_pick_rules: Maintain a denominator: count misses, unresolved claims and vague claims, not only hits.
Do not split one broad sentence into many successful predictions after the outcome.
Do not combine multiple failed alternatives into one later successful interpretation.
Do not award extra credit for details that were not fixed before the event.
Do not score a prediction against a source chosen only after seeing which source makes it appear correct.
Keep directional accuracy separate from magnitude accuracy.
A one-off hit does not establish stable predictive skill.
project_upgrade: Prophecy/revelation files should retain their theological meaning lane, while any claim presented as predictive receives a separate forecast record that can be scored without theology deciding the outcome.
